knowledge_point.title: Calculating Improper Integrals With an Unbounded Upper Limit Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we substitute $u=x + 1.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{d}u=1\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty$ when $x\to \infty,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=x + 1$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\infty$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\infty$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1992}{(x + 1)^{5}}\,\text{d}x=1992\int_{1}^{\infty}u^{-5}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1992}{(x + 1)^{5}}\,\text{d}x & =1992\lim_{a\to\infty}\int_{1}^{a}u^{-5}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\lim_{a\to\infty}\left[-498u^{-4}\right]_{1}^{a} \\ & =-498\lim_{a\to\infty}\left(a^{-4}-1\right) \\ & =-498\left(0-1\right) \\ & =498.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating Improper Integrals With an Unbounded Upper Limit Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we substitute $u=3 y + 2.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}y.
$$

Since $u\to \infty$ when $y\to \infty,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=3 y + 2$ is as follows:

| $y$ | $0$ | $\infty$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $\infty$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2625}{(3 y + 2)^{4}}\,\text{d}y=875\int_{2}^{\infty}u^{-4}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2625}{(3 y + 2)^{4}}\,\text{d}y & =875\lim_{a\to\infty}\int_{2}^{a}u^{-4}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\lim_{a\to\infty}\left[- \frac{875}{3}u^{-3}\right]_{2}^{a} \\ & =- \frac{875}{3}\lim_{a\to\infty}\left(a^{-3}-\frac{1}{8}\right) \\ & =- \frac{875}{3}\left(0-\frac{1}{8}\right) \\ & =\frac{875}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$
